# Sync integration tests

End-to-end tests for Actual's sync. Each test runs the **real sync server** and
two or more **real clients** ("devices"), and checks that the devices converge.

- The server is the real `sync-server` app, started in the test process on a
  free port, with its own temporary data directories.
- Each device is a full loot-core client (through `@actual-app/api`) in its own
  worker thread, with its own database, clock and prefs.
- Devices talk to the server over loopback HTTP only, and sync only when a test
  tells them to.

Use these tests to write sync scenarios: concurrent edits, offline catch-up,
and so on. They live in `packages/sync-server/integration-tests/` and run as
part of sync-server's `test` script, after its unit tests. The unit tests in
`packages/loot-core/src/server/sync/` (which use `mockSyncServer.ts`) and
`packages/sync-server/src/` are unchanged; these add coverage across both.

## Running the tests

From the repo root:

```bash
# As part of the whole suite. Builds @actual-app/api first (cached).
yarn test

# Just the integration tests. Needs a current API build; see the note below.
yarn build:api
yarn workspace @actual-app/sync-server run test:integration
```

Devices run on the **bundled** `@actual-app/api` build in `packages/api/dist`.
`yarn test` builds it (or restores it from lage's cache) before these tests.
When you run the integration tests directly, build it yourself after changing loot-core
or the API, and after any `yarn typecheck`: typecheck overwrites
`packages/api/dist/index.js` with an unbundled compile. If the bundle is
missing or overwritten, the tests stop right away and tell you to run
`yarn build:api`.

Requirements: Node 23.6 or newer (the device worker is a TypeScript file that
Node loads directly; the repo's `.nvmrc` pins a version that works).

## Writing a scenario

This is [`src/exampleScenario.test.ts`](src/exampleScenario.test.ts), which
runs with the rest of the suite:

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

import { assertInSync } from './assertInSync';
import { goOffline, goOnline, makeChange, sync } from './deviceHelpers';
import { setUpTwoDevices } from './setUpTwoDevices';
import type { TwoDevices } from './setUpTwoDevices';

describe('offline edits', () => {
  let setup: TwoDevices | undefined;

  afterEach(async () => {
    await setup?.tearDown();
    setup = undefined;
  });

  it('merges changes made while one device was offline', async () => {
    setup = await setUpTwoDevices();
    const { a, b } = setup;

    await goOffline(b);
    await makeChange(a, { type: 'createAccount', name: 'Checking' });
    await sync(a);
    await makeChange(b, { type: 'createAccount', name: 'Savings' });

    await goOnline(b);
    await sync(b); // sends Savings, receives Checking
    await sync(a); // receives Savings

    await assertInSync(a, b);
    const names = (await b.api<{ name: string }[]>('getAccounts')).map(
      account => account.name,
    );
    expect(names.sort()).toEqual(['Checking', 'Savings']);
  });
});
```

The pattern:

1. **Set up** with `setUpTwoDevices()`, and always tear down in `afterEach`
   (or `finally`), so the server and temporary files are cleaned up when a
   test fails.
2. **Change** devices with `makeChange`. Changes stay on that device.
3. **Sync** explicitly. Devices never sync on their own, so you decide the
   order. To fully converge, sync every device, then sync again any device
   that hasn't received the others' latest changes. With two devices,
   "A, B, A" always converges.
4. **Check** with `assertInSync(...devices)`, plus any specific `expect`s.

### Rules to know

- **One server per test file.** sync-server reads its config once, when its
  modules are first imported, so `startSyncServer()` can only run once per
  file. Several tests in a file can share one server (start it in
  `beforeAll`) and create fresh devices per test, as
  [`deviceHelpers.test.ts`](src/deviceHelpers.test.ts) does. Shared-server
  tests see each other's synced data, so don't assert exact totals across
  tests.
- **Nothing syncs implicitly.** loot-core normally starts a sync about a
  second after each change; test devices block that. Only `sync(device)` and
  the initial budget download reach the server.
- **Only loopback is reachable.** A device that tries any other host gets a
  network error, and the attempt is recorded
  (`device.request({ type: 'blockedRequests' })`).
- **Prefer the helpers to `device.api(...)` for changes.** `device.api` calls
  any `@actual-app/api` method and is fine for reading (`getAccounts`), but
  `makeChange` is where change types are defined for every scenario to share.

## Helper reference

| Helper                                                       | File                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `setUpTwoDevices()`                                          | `setUpTwoDevices.ts`           | Server with an uploaded budget, plus devices `a` and `b`. Returns `{ server, a, b, tearDown }`.                                                                              |
| `startSyncServerWithBudget()`                                | `startSyncServerWithBudget.ts` | Server, owner account, login token and uploaded starter budget. Returns `{ url, token, fileId, groupId, password, budgetId, budgetName, serverFiles, userFiles, shutdown }`. |
| `startSyncServer()`                                          | `startSyncServer.ts`           | Just the server, with temporary `serverFiles`/`userFiles` and migrations run. Returns `{ url, port, serverFiles, userFiles, shutdown }`.                                     |
| `createDevice(serverUrl, token, fileId, groupId, { name? })` | `createDevice.ts`              | A client in its own worker thread and data directory, signed in and with the budget downloaded. Use it for three or more devices.                                            |
| `makeChange(device, change)`                                 | `deviceHelpers.ts`             | Applies a change to that device's database only. Returns `{ id }`.                                                                                                           |
| `sync(device)`                                               | `deviceHelpers.ts`             | Runs one full sync (send, receive, repeat until device and server agree). Returns `{ received }`; throws on failure with loot-core's `reason`, e.g. `network-failure`.       |
| `goOffline(device)` / `goOnline(device)`                     | `deviceHelpers.ts`             | While offline, every request from the device fails like a dropped connection. Changes still work locally.                                                                    |
| `assertInSync(...devices)`                                   | `assertInSync.ts`              | Throws `OutOfSyncError` listing merkle hashes and the tables, rows and columns that differ.                                                                                  |
| `countServerMessages(server, groupId)`                       | `serverMessages.ts`            | How many sync messages the server has stored. Useful to check whether a change reached it.                                                                                   |

A `Device` also has `api(method, ...args)` and `send(handler, args)` (any
API method or internal loot-core handler), `getPrefs()`/`savePrefs()`,
`getClientId()` (its CRDT node id), `connection` and `close()`.

### What `assertInSync` compares

- Each device's **merkle root hash** against the server's. Equal hashes mean
  the same set of sync messages.
- Every row of every table that **any device has sync messages for**, matched
  by `id` and compared column by column (deleted rows included, via
  `tombstone`). Tables that are per device by design, such as caches, aren't
  compared, so they can't cause false failures.

It doesn't sync anything itself; call it after syncing. A failure looks like:

```text
Devices A, B are out of sync (group f545151c-…):

Merkle hashes (each device should match the server):
  server: 2083451566
  A: 2083451566 (14 messages)
  B: -1929899909 (7 messages)   <-- differs

Table "accounts": 1 row(s) differ
  row 9a54c33b-…: column "name" differs
    name: A="Everyday", B="Checking"
```

## Adding a change type

`makeChange` currently supports `createAccount`, `updateAccount` and
`deleteAccount`. To add one (say, a transaction):

1. Add a variant to `Change` in [`src/deviceProtocol.ts`](src/deviceProtocol.ts).
2. Handle it in `makeChange` in [`src/deviceWorker.ts`](src/deviceWorker.ts),
   using the `api` methods, and return `{ id }`. If you call an API method
   the devices haven't used before, add its signature to `ApiModule` in
   [`src/apiBundle.ts`](src/apiBundle.ts).

Keep values plain data (strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects): changes
and results are posted between threads.

## How it works

These answer the open questions from the issue that introduced these tests.

- **Why worker threads?** loot-core keeps its clock, database, prefs and sync
  state in module-level variables, so two clients in one module graph would
  share them. Each device runs in its own worker thread (its own module
  graph), which isolates them by construction.
- **Why `@actual-app/api`?** It already connects a loot-core client to a server
  (`init` with a session token, `downloadBudget`). Its bundled build runs in a
  plain worker thread, which loot-core's TypeScript source can't. No loot-core
  changes were needed.
- **Why the API is loaded by path.** sync-server doesn't depend on
  `@actual-app/api`, and adding that dependency (or a separate workspace for
  these tests) would change `yarn.lock`. So the device worker imports
  `packages/api/dist/index.js` by its repo path, and `src/apiBundle.ts` types
  the methods it calls. lage still builds the API before sync-server's tests.
  For the same reason, the starter budget is zipped by a small writer in
  `src/zip.ts` instead of a zip library.
- **Starting the server without building it.** Vitest compiles sync-server from
  source, including its `?raw` SQL imports and migration loading, so no
  sync-server build and no `--experimental-vm-modules` flag are needed. The
  changes to sync-server itself are that `src/app.ts` exports its Express
  `app` (plus a `#app` subpath import for it), so tests can listen on port 0
  and close the server afterwards.
- **How devices are controlled.** The worker wraps `fetch` before loading the
  API, which is how it blocks automatic syncs, simulates going offline, and
  refuses non-loopback hosts. Workers run with `NODE_ENV=production`, because
  in test mode loot-core syncs inside every change and throws if that fails.
- **Cleanup.** `shutdown()` and `close()` stop the server and workers, close
  their databases and delete their directories. `vitest.globalSetup.ts` also
  removes the temporary folders Vitest itself leaves behind on Windows.

## Troubleshooting

- **"…packages/api/dist/index.js is not the bundled build"**: run
  `yarn build:api`, then rerun. See [Running the tests](#running-the-tests).
- **A test times out while starting up**: startup is slow (several seconds per
  server, plus loot-core per device). Timeouts are 60s and at most two files
  run at once; see `integration-tests/vitest.config.ts`. A test that times out during startup
  can leave a temporary directory behind.
- **`[cause]: TypeError: fetch failed: automatic sync is disabled on test devices`**
  in the output is expected: it's loot-core logging an automatic sync that
  the device blocked.
- **`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')` from Vitest in
  every file**: an intermittent Vitest failure seen in several packages in
  this repo, not specific to these tests. Rerun.
````

import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

// Run by sync-server's `test` script after its unit tests, with
// `--config integration-tests/vitest.config.ts`. sync-server's own
// vitest.config.ts excludes this folder.
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    root: fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url)),
    include: ['src/**/*.test.ts'],
    environment: 'node',
    // Removes the temp folders Vitest itself leaves behind on Windows
    globalSetup: ['./vitest.globalSetup.ts'],
    // sync-server reads its config once at import, so each test file needs
    // its own module graph (and therefore its own server). Keep isolation on.
    isolate: true,
    // A cold import of the full sync-server app (every bank integration
    // included) plus migrations takes several seconds, and devices each load
    // all of loot-core. Setup often runs in `beforeAll`, so hooks get the
    // same budget as tests.
    testTimeout: 60_000,
    hookTimeout: 60_000,
    // Each file runs a server plus device worker threads. With every file
    // running at once (the default), setup took over 10s under `yarn test`;
    // two at a time keeps it well inside the timeouts
    maxWorkers: 2,
    reporters: process.env.CI
      ? [
          'default',
          [
            'junit',
            {
              // Next to sync-server's unit test results, where CI collects them
              outputFile: '../test-results/junit-integration.xml',
              suiteName: 'sync-server-integration',
            },
          ],
        ]
      : ['default'],
  },
});
=== vitest.globalSetup.ts
import { readFile, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

import type { TestProject } from 'vitest/node';

export async function setup(project: TestProject) {
  await assertApiBundleBuilt();

  const dirs = [project.tmpDir, Reflect.get(project.vitest, '_tmpDir')];
  return async function teardown() {
    await removeVitestTmpDirs(dirs);
  };
}

// Device workers load this file by path (see src/apiBundle.ts)
const API_BUNDLE = fileURLToPath(
  new URL('../../api/dist/index.js', import.meta.url),
);

/**
 * Devices run on the bundled `@actual-app/api` build, which inlines
 * loot-core. `yarn typecheck` overwrites that bundle with a plain compile
 * of `packages/api/index.ts` that imports loot-core's TypeScript source,
 * which a device can't load. `yarn test` rebuilds or restores the bundle
 * first; running these tests directly doesn't, so check here and
 * fail with the fix instead of a "Cannot find module" error in every test.
 */
async function assertApiBundleBuilt() {
  const code = await readFile(API_BUNDLE, 'utf8').catch(() => null);
  if (code === null || code.includes('@actual-app/core/')) {
    throw new Error(
      `${API_BUNDLE} is ${code === null ? 'missing' : 'not the bundled build'}. ` +
        'Run `yarn build:api` from the repo root, then run the tests again. ' +
        '(`yarn typecheck` overwrites the bundle; `yarn test` rebuilds it automatically.)',
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Vitest (5.0) copies transformed modules into folders directly under the
 * OS temp directory for its worker processes. It never removes its core
 * folder and only tries once to remove the project's, so on Windows every
 * run leaves at least one folder behind (this happens in every package in
 * the repo, not just this one). Remove this run's folders ourselves, so
 * the integration tests leave no temporary files.
 *
 * `_tmpDir` is internal to Vitest: only paths that are direct children of
 * the temp directory are removed, so if Vitest changes how it stores them
 * this does nothing rather than deleting the wrong thing.
 */
async function removeVitestTmpDirs(dirs: unknown[]) {
  const tempRoot = resolve(tmpdir());
  for (const dir of dirs) {
    if (typeof dir === 'string' && dirname(resolve(dir)) === tempRoot) {
      await rm(dir, {
        recursive: true,
        force: true,
        maxRetries: 5,
        retryDelay: 100,
      });
    }
  }
}

=== src/apiBundle.ts
// The parts of the built `@actual-app/api` that device workers use.
//
// sync-server doesn't depend on `@actual-app/api`, and adding the
// dependency would change yarn.lock, so devices load the built bundle by
// its path in the repo and these types describe the calls they make. If
// the API changes one of these signatures, update it here.
//
// Types only: deviceWorker.ts is loaded by Node
// directly and imports it with `import type`.

/** A row of a synced table, keyed by column name. */
type Row = Record<string, unknown>;

export type ApiSyncMessage = {
  timestamp: unknown;
  dataset: string;
  row: string;
  column: string;
  value: unknown;
};

export type ApiSyncResult =
  | { error: { reason: string; message?: string } }
  | { messages: ApiSyncMessage[] };

export type ApiPrefs = {
  id: string;
  cloudFileId?: string;
  groupId?: string;
};

/**
 * What `init` returns: loot-core's handler bridge and its database.
 * `send` is a plain function (it doesn't use `this`), so it's safe to pass
 * around on its own.
 */
export type ApiLib = {
  send(this: void, name: 'load-prefs'): Promise<ApiPrefs>;
  send(this: void, name: 'sync'): Promise<ApiSyncResult>;
  send(this: void, name: string, args?: unknown): Promise<unknown>;
  db: {
    all<T extends object = Row>(sql: string, params?: unknown[]): Promise<T[]>;
    first<T extends object = Row>(
      sql: string,
      params?: unknown[],
    ): Promise<T | null>;
  };
};

export type ApiModule = {
  init(config: {
    dataDir: string;
    serverURL: string;
    sessionToken: string;
  }): Promise<ApiLib>;
  downloadBudget(syncId: string): Promise<void>;
  createAccount(
    account: { name: string; offbudget: boolean },
    initialBalance: number,
  ): Promise<string>;
  updateAccount(
    id: string,
    fields: { name?: string; offbudget?: boolean; closed?: boolean },
  ): Promise<void>;
  deleteAccount(id: string): Promise<void>;
  shutdown(): Promise<void>;
};

import { mkdtemp, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
import type { Server } from 'node:http';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';

export type SyncServerHandle = {
  url: string;
  port: number;
  serverFiles: string;
  userFiles: string;
  shutdown: () => Promise<void>;
};

let hasStarted = false;

/**
 * Starts the real sync-server app in this process on a random free port,
 * with fresh temporary `serverFiles` and `userFiles` directories.
 *
 * sync-server loads its config once, when its modules are first imported,
 * so this can only be called once per module graph (i.e. once per test
 * file under Vitest's default isolation).
 */
export async function startSyncServer(): Promise<SyncServerHandle> {
  if (hasStarted) {
    throw new Error(
      'startSyncServer() was already called in this module graph. ' +
        'sync-server reads its config once at import; use one server per test file.',
    );
  }
  hasStarted = true;

  const rootDir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'actual-sync-server-'));
  const serverFiles = join(rootDir, 'server-files');
  const userFiles = join(rootDir, 'user-files');

  // The migration state file lives in `dataDir`, so it must be temporary
  // too: a stale state file elsewhere would make migrations skip creating
  // the tables in the fresh account.sqlite. The config path points at a
  // file that doesn't exist so no developer config.json is picked up.
  const restoreEnv = setEnv({
    ACTUAL_CONFIG_PATH: join(rootDir, 'config.json'),
    ACTUAL_DATA_DIR: rootDir,
    ACTUAL_SERVER_FILES: serverFiles,
    ACTUAL_USER_FILES: userFiles,
  });

  let server: Server | undefined;
  try {
    // Migrations must run before the app is imported: the app's modules
    // touch the account database as they load.
    const { run: runMigrations } = await import('#migrations');
    await runMigrations();

    const { app } = await import('#app');
    server = await listen(app.listen(0, '127.0.0.1'));
  } catch (error) {
    await removeDir(rootDir);
    throw error;
  } finally {
    restoreEnv();
  }

  const address = server.address();
  if (address === null || typeof address === 'string') {
    throw new Error('Expected the sync server to listen on a TCP port');
  }

  const { closeAccountDb } = await import('#account-db');
  const listeningServer = server;
  let shutdownPromise: Promise<void> | null = null;

  return {
    url: `http://127.0.0.1:${address.port}`,
    port: address.port,
    serverFiles,
    userFiles,
    shutdown() {
      shutdownPromise ??= (async () => {
        await closeServer(listeningServer);
        // Windows can't delete account.sqlite while it is still open
        closeAccountDb();
        await removeDir(rootDir);
      })();
      return shutdownPromise;
    },
  };
}

function setEnv(values: Record<string, string>): () => void {
  const previous = Object.fromEntries(
    Object.keys(values).map(key => [key, process.env[key]]),
  );
  Object.assign(process.env, values);

  return () => {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(previous)) {
      if (value === undefined) {
        delete process.env[key];
      } else {
        process.env[key] = value;
      }
    }
  };
}

function listen(server: Server): Promise<Server> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once('listening', () => resolve(server));
    server.once('error', reject);
  });
}

function closeServer(server: Server): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.close(error => (error ? reject(error) : resolve()));
    // Drop keep-alive connections so close() doesn't wait on them
    server.closeAllConnections();
  });
}

function removeDir(dir: string): Promise<void> {
  return rm(dir, {
    recursive: true,
    force: true,
    maxRetries: 5,
    retryDelay: 100,
  });
}

    25	// --- Network gate -------------------------------------------------------
    26	//
    27	// loot-core's API build captures `globalThis.fetch` when it loads, so the
    28	// gate has to be installed before `@actual-app/api` is imported.
    29	//
    30	// - Offline: every request fails like a dropped connection, which loot-core
    31	//   reports as `network-failure`.
    32	// - Online: requests go through, except sync requests that don't come from
    33	//   an explicit `sync` op. loot-core normally starts a sync after every
    34	//   local change; blocking those keeps `makeChange` local and makes `sync`
    35	//   the only way data reaches the server, so tests stay deterministic.
    36	// - Always: only loopback hosts are reachable. Anything else is refused and
    37	//   recorded, so tests can assert the device never touched a real network.
    38	const realFetch = globalThis.fetch;
    39	const LOOPBACK_HOSTS = new Set(['127.0.0.1', 'localhost', '[::1]']);
    40	const blockedRequests: string[] = [];
    41	let isOnline = true;
    42	let explicitSyncsRunning = 0;

    44	globalThis.fetch = (input, init) => {

   223	async function getSnapshot(tableNames: string[]): Promise<DeviceSnapshot> {
   224	  const { db } = requireLib();
   225	  const clockRow = await db.first<{ clock: string }>(
   226	    'SELECT clock FROM messages_clock WHERE id = 1',
   227	  );
   228	  const merkleHash = clockRow
   229	    ? (JSON.parse(clockRow.clock).merkle?.hash ?? 0)
   230	    : 0;
   231	  const countRow = await db.first<{ count: number }>(
   232	    'SELECT count(*) AS count FROM messages_crdt',
   233	  );
   234	
   235	  const tables: Record<string, TableRow[]> = {};
   236	  for (const table of tableNames) {
   237	    // Table names come from the CRDT log; quote them like loot-core does
   238	    const quoted = `"${table.replaceAll('"', '""')}"`;
   239	    tables[table] = await db.all<TableRow>(
   240	      `SELECT * FROM ${quoted} ORDER BY id`,
   241	    );
   242	  }
   243	
   244	  return { merkleHash, messageCount: countRow?.count ?? 0, tables };
   245	}

   248	  const row = await requireLib().db.first<{ clock: string }>(
   249	    'SELECT clock FROM messages_clock WHERE id = 1',
   250	  );
   251	  if (!row) {
   252	    throw new Error('This device has no clock yet');
   253	  }
   254	  // A serialized timestamp ends in the 16-hex-digit node id
   255	  const { timestamp } = JSON.parse(row.clock);
   256	  return String(timestamp).split('-').pop() ?? '';

   270	  // loot-core uses `reason` on its own errors and `code` on API errors
   271	  const reason = Reflect.get(error, 'reason') ?? Reflect.get(error, 'code');
   272	  return {
   273	    message: error.message,
   274	    stack: error.stack,
   275	    reason: typeof reason === 'string' ? reason : undefined,
   276	  };

    42	/**

    61	  // changes. Automatic syncs are blocked in the worker instead.
    62	  const worker = new Worker(new URL('./deviceWorker.ts', import.meta.url), {
    63	    execArgv: [],

    19	  return device.request({ type: 'makeChange', change });
    20	}
    21	
    22	/**
    23	 * Runs one full sync cycle (send local changes, receive and apply remote
    24	 * ones, repeat until the device and server agree). Throws on failure; the
    25	 * error's `reason` is loot-core's, e.g. `network-failure` when offline.
    26	 */
    27	export function sync(device: Device): Promise<SyncResult> {
    28	  return device.request({ type: 'sync' });
    29	}
    30	
    31	/** Makes every request from the device fail as if it had no connection. */
    32	export async function goOffline(device: Device): Promise<void> {
    33	  await device.request({ type: 'setOnline', online: false });
    34	}
    35	
    36	/** Lets the device reach the server again. */
    37	export async function goOnline(device: Device): Promise<void> {
    38	  await device.request({ type: 'setOnline', online: true });
    39	}

    11	import type { Device, DeviceConnection } from './createDevice';
    12	import type { DeviceSnapshot, TableRow } from './deviceProtocol';
    13	
    14	// How many differing rows to print per table before summarizing the rest
    15	const MAX_ROWS_PER_TABLE = 10;
    16	
    17	// Sorts after every real timestamp, so the server sends no messages back
    18	const FAR_FUTURE_SINCE = '9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z-0000-0000000000000000';
    19	
    20	export class OutOfSyncError extends Error {
    21	  override name = 'OutOfSyncError';
    22	}
    23	
    24	/**
    25	 * Checks that every device holds the same synced data and the same set of
    26	 * sync messages as the server. Compares:
    27	 *
    28	 * - each device's merkle root hash with the server's, and
    29	 * - every row of every table any device has sync messages for.
    30	 *
    31	 * Throws an `OutOfSyncError` listing the hashes and the specific tables,
    32	 * rows and columns that differ. Call it after syncing; it doesn't sync.
    33	 */
    34	export async function assertInSync(...devices: Device[]): Promise<void> {
    35	  if (devices.length < 1) {
    36	    throw new Error('assertInSync needs at least one device');
    37	  }
    38	  const connection = sameConnection(devices);
    39	
    40	  const tableLists = await Promise.all(
    41	    devices.map(device => device.request<string[]>({ type: 'syncedTables' })),
    42	  );
    43	  const tables = [...new Set(tableLists.flat())].sort();
    44	
    45	  const [serverHash, snapshots] = await Promise.all([
    46	    fetchServerMerkleHash(connection),
    47	    Promise.all(
    48	      devices.map(device =>
    49	        device.request<DeviceSnapshot>({ type: 'snapshot', tables }),
    50	      ),
    51	    ),
    52	  ]);
    53	
    54	  const problems = [
    55	    ...compareHashes(devices, snapshots, serverHash),
    56	    ...tables.flatMap(table => compareTable(table, devices, snapshots)),
    57	  ];
    58	
    59	  if (problems.length > 0) {
    60	    const names = devices.map(device => device.name).join(', ');
    61	    throw new OutOfSyncError(
    62	      [
    63	        `Devices ${names} are out of sync (group ${connection.groupId}):`,
    64	        '',
    65	        ...problems,
    66	      ].join('\n'),
    67	    );
    68	  }
    69	}
    70	
    71	function sameConnection(devices: Device[]): DeviceConnection {
    72	  const [first] = devices;
    73	  const mismatched = devices.find(
    74	    device =>
    75	      device.connection.serverUrl !== first.connection.serverUrl ||
    76	      device.connection.groupId !== first.connection.groupId,
    77	  );
    78	  if (mismatched) {
    79	    throw new Error(
    80	      `assertInSync: ${mismatched.name} syncs a different server or budget than ${first.name}`,
    81	    );
    82	  }
    83	  return first.connection;
    84	}
    85	
    86	/** Asks the server for its merkle via an empty sync request. */
    87	async function fetchServerMerkleHash({
    88	  serverUrl,
    89	  token,
    90	  fileId,
    91	  groupId,
    92	}: DeviceConnection): Promise<number> {
    93	  const request = create(SyncRequestSchema, {
    94	    fileId,
    95	    groupId,
    96	    since: FAR_FUTURE_SINCE,
    97	    messages: [],
    98	  });
    99	  const res = await fetch(`${serverUrl}/sync/sync`, {
   100	    method: 'POST',
   101	    headers: {
   102	      'Content-Type': 'application/actual-sync',
   103	      'X-ACTUAL-TOKEN': token,
   104	    },
   105	    body: toBinary(SyncRequestSchema, request),
   106	  });
   107	  if (!res.ok) {
   108	    throw new Error(
   109	      `assertInSync: server sync request failed (${res.status}): ${await res.text()}`,
   110	    );
   111	  }
   112	  const response = fromBinary(
   113	    SyncResponseSchema,
   114	    new Uint8Array(await res.arrayBuffer()),
   115	  );
   116	  return JSON.parse(response.merkle).hash ?? 0;
   117	}
   118	
   119	function compareHashes(
   120	  devices: Device[],
   121	  snapshots: DeviceSnapshot[],
   122	  serverHash: number,
   123	): string[] {
   124	  const allMatch = snapshots.every(s => s.merkleHash === serverHash);
   125	  if (allMatch) {
   126	    return [];
   127	  }
   128	  return [
   129	    'Merkle hashes (each device should match the server):',
   130	    `  server: ${serverHash}`,
   131	    ...devices.map((device, i) => {
   132	      const { merkleHash, messageCount } = snapshots[i];
   133	      const mark = merkleHash === serverHash ? '' : '   <-- differs';
   134	      return `  ${device.name}: ${merkleHash} (${messageCount} messages)${mark}`;
   135	    }),
   136	    '',
   137	  ];
   138	}
   139	
   140	function compareTable(
   141	  table: string,
   142	  devices: Device[],
   143	  snapshots: DeviceSnapshot[],
   144	): string[] {
   145	  const rowsByDevice = snapshots.map(
   146	    snapshot =>
   147	      new Map((snapshot.tables[table] ?? []).map(row => [row.id, row])),
   148	  );
   149	  const ids = [
   150	    ...new Set(rowsByDevice.flatMap(rows => [...rows.keys()])),
   151	  ].sort();
   152	
   153	  const rowProblems: string[][] = [];
   154	  for (const id of ids) {
   155	    const rows = rowsByDevice.map(byId => byId.get(id));
   156	    const problem = describeRowDifference(id, devices, rows);
   157	    if (problem) {
   158	      rowProblems.push(problem);
   159	    }
   160	  }
   161	
   162	  if (rowProblems.length === 0) {
   163	    return [];
   164	  }
   165	  const shown = rowProblems.slice(0, MAX_ROWS_PER_TABLE).flat();
   166	  const hidden = rowProblems.length - MAX_ROWS_PER_TABLE;
   167	  return [
   168	    `Table "${table}": ${rowProblems.length} row(s) differ`,
   169	    ...shown,
   170	    ...(hidden > 0 ? [`  ...and ${hidden} more row(s)`] : []),
   171	    '',
   172	  ];
   173	}
   174	
   175	function describeRowDifference(
   176	  id: string,
   177	  devices: Device[],
   178	  rows: Array<TableRow | undefined>,
   179	): string[] | null {
   180	  const missingOn = devices.filter((_, i) => rows[i] === undefined);
   181	  if (missingOn.length > 0) {
   182	    const presentOn = devices.filter((_, i) => rows[i] !== undefined);
   183	    return [
   184	      `  row ${id}: only on ${names(presentOn)}, missing on ${names(missingOn)}`,
   185	      ...presentOn.map(
   186	        device =>
   187	          `    ${device.name}: ${format(rows[devices.indexOf(device)])}`,
   188	      ),
   189	    ];
   190	  }
   191	
   192	  const columns = [
   193	    ...new Set(rows.flatMap(row => Object.keys(row ?? {}))),
   194	  ].sort();
   195	  const differing = columns.filter(column =>
   196	    rows.some(row => !isDeepStrictEqual(row?.[column], rows[0]?.[column])),
   197	  );
   198	  if (differing.length === 0) {
   199	    return null;
   200	  }
   201	  return [
   202	    `  row ${id}: ${differing.length === 1 ? 'column' : 'columns'} ${differing
   203	      .map(column => `"${column}"`)
   204	      .join(', ')} ${differing.length === 1 ? 'differs' : 'differ'}`,
   205	    ...differing.map(
   206	      column =>
   207	        `    ${column}: ${devices
   208	          .map((device, i) => `${device.name}=${format(rows[i]?.[column])}`)
   209	          .join(', ')}`,
   210	    ),
   211	  ];
   212	}
   213	
   214	function names(devices: Device[]): string {
   215	  return devices.map(device => device.name).join(', ');
   216	}
   217	
   218	function format(value: unknown): string {
   219	  return JSON.stringify(value) ?? String(value);
   220	}

=== zip.ts
     1	import { crc32 } from 'node:zlib';
     2	
     3	// 1980-01-01, the earliest date a zip file can store
     4	const DOS_DATE = (0 << 9) | (1 << 5) | 1;
     5	
     6	/**
     7	 * Builds a zip archive with uncompressed ("stored") entries: just enough
     8	 * to hand a budget to the client, which unzips it with fflate. Written
     9	 * out by hand so the tests don't need a zip library as a dependency.
    10	 */
    11	export function zipStored(files: Record<string, Uint8Array>): Uint8Array {
    12	  const localParts: Buffer[] = [];
    13	  const centralParts: Buffer[] = [];
    14	  let offset = 0;
    15	
    16	  for (const [name, data] of Object.entries(files)) {
    17	    const nameBytes = Buffer.from(name, 'utf8');
    18	    const checksum = crc32(data);
    19	
    20	    const local = Buffer.alloc(30);
    21	    local.writeUInt32LE(0x04034b50, 0); // local file header signature
    22	    local.writeUInt16LE(20, 4); // version needed to extract
    23	    local.writeUInt16LE(0, 6); // flags
    24	    local.writeUInt16LE(0, 8); // compression: stored
    25	    local.writeUInt16LE(0, 10); // modification time
    26	    local.writeUInt16LE(DOS_DATE, 12); // modification date
    27	    local.writeUInt32LE(checksum, 14);
    28	    local.writeUInt32LE(data.length, 18); // compressed size
    29	    local.writeUInt32LE(data.length, 22); // uncompressed size
    30	    local.writeUInt16LE(nameBytes.length, 26);
    31	    local.writeUInt16LE(0, 28); // extra field length
    32	
    33	    const central = Buffer.alloc(46);
    34	    central.writeUInt32LE(0x02014b50, 0); // central directory signature
    35	    central.writeUInt16LE(20, 4); // version made by
    36	    central.writeUInt16LE(20, 6); // version needed to extract
    37	    central.writeUInt16LE(0, 8); // flags
    38	    central.writeUInt16LE(0, 10); // compression: stored
    39	    central.writeUInt16LE(0, 12); // modification time
    40	    central.writeUInt16LE(DOS_DATE, 14); // modification date
    41	    central.writeUInt32LE(checksum, 16);
    42	    central.writeUInt32LE(data.length, 20); // compressed size
    43	    central.writeUInt32LE(data.length, 24); // uncompressed size
    44	    central.writeUInt16LE(nameBytes.length, 28);
    45	    // extra length, comment length, disk number, internal and external
    46	    // attributes stay 0
    47	    central.writeUInt32LE(offset, 42); // offset of the local header
    48	
    49	    localParts.push(local, nameBytes, Buffer.from(data));
    50	    centralParts.push(central, nameBytes);
    51	    offset += local.length + nameBytes.length + data.length;
    52	  }
    53	
    54	  const centralDirectory = Buffer.concat(centralParts);
    55	  const count = Object.keys(files).length;
    56	  const end = Buffer.alloc(22);
    57	  end.writeUInt32LE(0x06054b50, 0); // end of central directory signature
    58	  end.writeUInt16LE(count, 8); // entries on this disk
    59	  end.writeUInt16LE(count, 10); // total entries
    60	  end.writeUInt32LE(centralDirectory.length, 12);
    61	  end.writeUInt32LE(offset, 16); // offset of the central directory
    62	
    63	  return new Uint8Array(Buffer.concat([...localParts, centralDirectory, end]));
    64	}

    12	export function countServerMessages(
    13	  server: SyncServerHandle,
    14	  groupId: string,
    15	): number {
    16	  const path = join(server.userFiles, `group-${groupId}.sqlite`);
    17	  if (!existsSync(path)) {

    19	  }
    20	  const db = openDatabase(path);
    21	  try {

    23	  } finally {
    24	    db.close();
    25	  }
    26	}

    32	    devices.push(

    34	    );
    35	  } catch (error) {
    36	    await tearDown();

    38	  }

10	
11	Cumulative rules as of Sprint 3 (2026-11). Graded per PR out of 20: implements ACs 6 · tests + Test Evidence 6 · what/why + Tech Debt + linked issue 3 · CI or manual verification 3 · rubric review + approval on latest commit 2.
12	
13	**Why:** these are graded line by line, and missing sections cost points even when the code is right.
14	**How to apply:** run through this list whenever drafting a branch, commit, PR body, or review.
15	
16	## Branch & commit
17	
18	- One branch per issue, cut from an up-to-date `master` (the course site says `main`; this repo uses `master`). Names: `feat/issue-<n>-<slug>`, `fix/issue-<n>-<slug>`.
19	- Commit: conventional prefix + issue number, e.g. `feat: add PDF export for reports (#42)`. The repo's agent rules also require an `[AI]` prefix on commits and PR titles made by an agent, so `[AI] feat: … (#42)`.
20	- Never push to `master` (it's protected). After merging, switch to `master`, pull, and delete the branch locally and on GitHub.
21	
22	## PR body (all required)
23	
24	1. `Closes #<issue>` (course wording; upstream uses `Fixes #` — `Closes` is fine). Attach the PR to the `Sprint N` milestone.
25	2. **What changed and why**, in the student's own words.
26	3. **Tech Debt** section with both fields: **Introduced:** (shortcuts or compromises made here, and why) and **Encountered:** (pre-existing debt met, and how it was handled). Write "None." when there is none.
27	4. **Test Evidence** section (S3+, replaces "how it was tested"):
28	   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
29	   - One row per AC from the issue (for bugs, use the Expected Behavior instead). If there's no product behavior change (CI-only, etc.), write N/A and explain.
30	   - Test(s): test name + file; manual checks are written `Manual: <steps> → <result>`; list both if an AC is covered both ways.
31	   - Level: `unit` / `integration` / `E2E` / `manual`.
32	   - Source: `AC` / `issue discussion` / `docs` / `upstream behavior` / `other (explain)`. **The current output of our own code is never a valid source.**
33	   - Plus: **Not tested automatically, and why** (manual rows only), and **AI-written tests**: list tests AI wrote or changed and how their expected values were verified ("None" if none).
34	5. CI result. If CI isn't running, list the commands run and their pass/fail/skip counts (`yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint`, the workspace test command).
35	6. New or updated tests for every behavior change.
36	
37	- Upstream Definition of Done (docs/sprint0/standards.md) also expects `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint:fix`, and passing tests to be run, plus a release note in `upcoming-release-notes/` (use the writing-release-notes skill).
38	- **Conflict to raise with the user:** `.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md` says agents should leave the PR template unfilled, but the course grades the PR body. Draft the course sections for the user and ask how they want them placed, rather than silently following either rule.
39	
40	## Review & merge
41	
42	- No self-approval or self-merge. At least one teammate approves; **merge only if that approval is on the latest commit** (any push after approval needs a new approval).
43	- Request the review on GitHub and ping the reviewer on Zulip. Reviewers reply within 24h.
44	- The reviewer posts a **rubric comment during the first review pass**, before the author revises, scoring 1–10 with a 1–2 sentence note each: Correctness · Test coverage · Code quality · Documentation · AI transparency (evidence of human verification) · **Test evidence** (S3: does every AC have a test, are expected values justified, which tests did the reviewer run locally) · Overall (merge as-is?). "LGTM" or approval alone doesn't count.

Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally?", "Overall — would you merge this as-is?". Line-specific comments go in GitHub's code review UI. A follow-up revision may add a brief update noting what changed.

[AI] feat: first attempt at sync server tests (#161)
sgstrick
None
## Description

Adds a test-only workspace, `packages/sync-integration-tests`, that runs the real sync server and two or more real clients in one test. Until now, no test exercised a real client against a real server: loot-core's sync tests replace the server with `mockSyncServer.ts`, and sync-server's `app-sync.test.ts` calls endpoints without a client. Includes server setup helpers, isolated client devices via worker threads, sync/offline helpers, an `assertInSync` comparator, a smoke test, and a README. One small change outside the new package: `packages/sync-server/src/app.ts` now exports its Express `app` so tests can bind to port 0 and close the server cleanly; production startup via `run()` is unchanged. No loot-core code changed.

AI Logs will be posted at the end of the sprint.


## Related issue(s)

Closes #161 . Groundwork for #162 , which depends on it.


## Testing

- 13 tests across 8 files, each isolating one piece before combining them.
- startSyncServer.test.ts: Server starts on a free port, /health responds, temp directories are removed after shutdown.
- startSyncServerWithBudget.test.ts: Account creation, login, and budget upload return a valid token, fileId, and groupId.
- createDevice.test.ts: Two devices have separate data directories, CRDT node IDs, prefs, and databases.
- createDevice.sync.test.ts: After sync, B has A's account data but not A's local prefs.
- deviceHelpers.test.ts: makeChange stays local; sync pushes changes; goOffline makes sync throw; goOnline delivers offline changes.
- assertInSync.test.ts: Passes when synced; reports missing rows and stale columns with readable output.
- e2e.smoke.test.ts: A change on A appears on B after both sync, with no non-loopback network requests and no files left behind.
- exampleScenario.test.ts: The README walkthrough kept as a live test so docs can't drift.
- Full suite (yarn test:debug) passed all 13 targets including loot-core's existing sync tests (54 passed, 2 skipped by pre-existing it.skip). yarn typecheck passes. Known caveat: only run on Windows so far — confirm CI (Linux) result once it runs.


## Design Decisions

- Clients run in worker threads. Considered: same-process module resets via vi.resetModules(), child processes, or worker threads. loot-core's clock, database, prefs, and sync state are module-level globals, so a separate module graph per client is the only option that isolates them by construction; module resets risk silently missing a shared global, and child processes add startup cost without additional isolation. Consequence: devices are driven by message passing and load the built API bundle rather than loot-core source.
- Clients use @actual-app/api. Considered: calling loot-core internals directly, loading loot-core from source in the worker, or using the bundled API. The API already supports token-based login and budget download, and its bundle runs in a plain worker without TypeScript tooling. Consequence: no loot-core changes required, but tests need a current API build.
- Setup lives in a new workspace. Considered: colocating inside loot-core, inside sync-server, or in a new package. The setup depends on both client and server; placing it in either would create a circular dependency, and a separate package also keeps these slower tests out of loot-core's fast suite. Consequence: one additional workspace in lage, the root tsconfig, and yarn.lock.
- Tests run on every yarn test. Considered: an opt-in yarn test:integration script or including in the default suite. An opt-in script is easy to forget and lets the setup rot; running by default keeps it honest. Consequence: roughly 30-40s added to the suite plus the API build cost (cached when loot-core is unchanged).
- Devices sync only when the test calls sync(). Considered: allowing loot-core's 1-second automatic sync, using NODE_ENV=test to sync inside each change, or explicit test-controlled syncing. Automatic syncing makes event ordering nondeterministic; test mode makes offline scenarios impossible. Consequence: scenarios must state every sync explicitly, and workers run with NODE_ENV=production.
- assertInSync compares only synced tables. Considered: comparing every table in the budget database or only CRDT-logged tables plus merkle hashes. Per-device tables such as caches differ legitimately and would cause false failures. Consequence: a table that never produces sync messages is not compared.


## Tech Debt

Introduced:
- sync-server exports app only because run() discards the server handle and has no shutdown path; tests need the app object directly.
- Offline simulation depends on the API bundle reading globalThis.fetch at load time; if that changes, offline toggling and the sync block silently stop working.
- assertInSync uses _tmpDir, a Vitest internal, for temp folder cleanup; guarded to no-op if the value doesn't look like a temp path.
- One sync server per test file, because sync-server reads its config once on import.
- A test that times out during server startup can leave a temporary directory behind.
- makeChange supports accounts only; #162 will need transactions, categories, and other entity types.
- The device worker is TypeScript loaded directly by Node, requiring Node 23.6+; .nvmrc pins 24 but engines allows 22.
- 60s timeouts and a cap of 2 concurrent test files, because each file starts a server and loads loot-core per device.

Encountered:
- Module-level globals in loot-core (clock, database, prefs, sync mode) make multiple clients in one process impossible; worked around with worker threads rather than refactoring loot-core.
- yarn typecheck overwrites packages/api/dist/index.js with an unbundled compile, replacing the bundle from yarn build:api; this package now detects the missing bundle and exits with a clear message. Root fix (setting emitDeclarationOnly in that tsconfig) is out of scope and owned by a different team.
- Vitest 5.0 leaks a temp folder on every run on Windows across all packages; this package cleans up its own, but others still leak.
- Intermittent Vitest runner failures (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')) appeared once across a full run and were not reproduced in roughly 12 subsequent runs; cause unknown.
- yarn lint fails on Windows due to CRLF line endings in 505 existing files unrelated to this PR; left as-is.


## Checklist
- [X] Release notes added (see link above)
- [X] No obvious regressions in affected areas
- [X] Self-review has been performed - I have read every line of this diff and can explain what each change does and why it is needed

ISSUE: [AI] Add testing scenarios for real sync testing
None
## Summary
Using the test setup from issue A, this issue adds end-to-end tests for the situations where syncing between devices usually goes wrong: edits made at the same time, a device that has been offline for a long time, a sync reset while another device is still syncing, and encrypted budgets. Each test runs real clients against a real sync server and checks that every device ends up with the same data and the same merkle hash as the server. Today none of these cases is tested end to end. The existing client tests use a mocked server (`mockSyncServer.ts`), so a change to the client or server sync code could break real multi-device sync without any test failing.

## User Story
As a developer changing Actual's sync code, I want tests for the realistic ways devices fall out of step, so that I find out before merging if my change causes devices to end up with different data or get stuck with an `out-of-sync` error.

## User Scenario
A developer changes how the client sends messages to the server and runs `yarn test`. The integration suite runs each scenario. In one, device B goes offline, makes 500 edits, comes back online and syncs. In another, A and B both rename the same category before either one syncs. If the change breaks anything, the failing test names the scenario and shows which tables or merkle hashes differ, so the developer knows where to look.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. **Basic sync both ways:** changes made on A appear on B, and changes made on B appear on A.
2. **Edits at the same time:** A and B change the same field before either one syncs. After both sync, both devices hold the same value, and it is the one with the later timestamp.
3. **Different records at the same time:** A and B each add and delete different transactions while out of contact. After syncing, both devices have every change.
4. **Offline catch-up:** B makes a large number of changes (hundreds or more) while offline, then reconnects. Both devices end up in sync with no `out-of-sync` error. Note in the test how large a batch it handles before the server's size limit (`upload.fileSizeSyncLimitMB`) gets in the way.
5. **Sync reset:** A resets sync, which gives the file a new `groupId`. B then tries to sync. B detects the reset and does not apply messages from the old group (see the `groupId` check in `_fullSync`, `packages/loot-core/src/server/sync/index.ts`).
6. **Encrypted file:** scenarios 1 and 2 pass with end-to-end encryption turned on, and a device with the wrong key gets a decrypt error instead of corrupted data.
7. Every scenario ends with the `assertInSync` helper from 6a. Scenarios that fail because of real bugs are marked skipped or known-failing, with a link to a separate bug issue.
8. The whole suite finishes in a reasonable time (aim for under about 60 seconds) and runs in CI.

## Rough Scope
Medium. Once issue #161 is done, each scenario is a fairly short test. The time goes into understanding the expected behaviour: how the client resolves edits made at the same time (by timestamp), what a sync reset does to other devices, and how encryption keys get to a second device. Expect some scenarios to expose real bugs that need their own issues.

## Out of Scope
- Building the test setup (issue A).
- Fixing bugs these tests find. File each one as its own issue.
- Batching large uploads. The offline catch-up test may show that this is needed, but implementing it is a separate issue.
- Clock-drift testing, load or performance testing, and bank-sync integrations.

## Open Questions
- What counts as "the same data" when comparing devices? Should the check cover only user-facing tables (transactions, categories, payees, etc.), or also internal tables such as `messages_crdt`?
- How large an offline batch should the catch-up test use: just under the server's size limit, or over it, with the test marked known-failing until upload batching is done?
- How does a second device get the encryption key in a test? Does it need the user's password entered again, or can it reuse the key?
- Should the expected behaviour after a sync reset be documented somewhere as well as tested?

## Source
Follows on from issue #161. Found by our team while reading the sync code (`packages/loot-core/src/server/sync/index.ts`, `packages/sync-server/src/sync-simple.js`). These scenarios cover the cases most likely to break if we later add upload batching, `/sync` input validation or real-time change notifications.

ISSUE: [AI] Build the test setup for sync server testing
## Acceptance Criteria
1. A setup helper that:
   - starts the real `sync-server` app in-process on a free port, with temporary `serverFiles` and `userFiles` directories
   - creates an account or session and returns a valid token
   - uploads an initial budget file and returns its `fileId` and `groupId`
   - shuts everything down and removes the temporary files afterwards, even when a test fails
2. A way to create at least two independent client instances that point at that server and don't share sync state (prefs, clock, open database).
3. Helpers:
   - `makeChange(device, …)`: makes a change on one device
   - `sync(device)`: runs a full sync and returns or throws the result
   - `goOffline(device)` and `goOnline(device)`
   - `assertInSync(...devices)`: checks that the budget database tables match across devices and that every device's merkle hash matches the server's
4. One smoke test that proves the setup works: a change on A appears on B after both sync.
5. Runs under `yarn test` (or a documented separate script; see Open Questions) with no network access, and the existing unit tests and `mockSyncServer.ts` keep working unchanged.
6. A short README or comment explaining how to use the helpers to write a new scenario.

## Rough Scope
Medium. The main difficulty is running more than one client. loot-core keeps sync state (`prefs`, `getClock()`, `db`) in module-level variables, so two clients in one process may need separate workers or processes, or `vi.resetModules()`-style isolation. Starting the server from tests may also need config changes, because its test script uses `--experimental-vm-modules` and `sync-simple.js` imports SQL with `?raw`. The work touches `packages/sync-server` (the app and its config), `packages/loot-core` (the sync client and the `post` and `cloud-storage` layer), and the test and lage setup. It doesn't touch the UI.

## Out of Scope
- The full set of sync scenarios (edits at the same time, offline catch-up, sync reset, encryption). Those are issue B.
- Fixing sync bugs the setup finds. File each one separately.
- UI or Playwright end-to-end tests, load testing, and bank-sync integrations.

## Open Questions
- Can two loot-core clients run in one Node process, or does each need its own worker or process?
- Where should the setup live: in `loot-core`, in `sync-server`, or in a new test-only workspace that depends on both?
- Can the sync server be started from tests without building it first?
- Should the client side go through `@actual-app/api` (which already supports connecting to a server) instead of loot-core internals?
- Should this run on every `yarn test` or behind a separate `yarn test:integration` script?

## Source
Found by our team while reading the sync code (`packages/loot-core/src/server/sync/index.ts`, `packages/sync-server/src/app-sync.ts`, `packages/sync-server/src/sync-simple.js`). This is groundwork for issue #162 and for other sync work we're considering (batching large uploads, validating input on `/sync`, real-time change notifications).

[AI] feat: first attempt at sync server tests (#161)
milestone: None
head: 9806dd096
## Description

Adds a test setup for end-to-end sync tests: a real sync server and two or more real clients ("devices") in one test, with helpers to change, sync and compare devices. Until now no test ran a real client against a real server. The loot-core sync tests use `mockSyncServer.ts`, and `app-sync.test.ts` tests the server endpoints with no client. This setup is the groundwork for the sync scenarios in #162.

**What's included** (all in `packages/sync-server/integration-tests/`):

- **Server:** `startSyncServer()` starts the real sync-server app in the test process on a free port, with temporary `serverFiles`/`userFiles`. `startSyncServerWithBudget()` also creates the account, logs in, and uploads a starter budget, returning `token`, `fileId` and `groupId`. `shutdown()` stops the server and deletes its directories.
- **Devices:** `createDevice()` gives each client its own worker thread and data directory, so devices don't share prefs, clock or database. Each device is a full loot-core client through `@actual-app/api`.
- **Helpers:** `makeChange`, `sync`, `goOffline`/`goOnline`, `assertInSync`, plus `setUpTwoDevices()` for the common case. Devices only talk to loopback hosts and never sync on their own, so tests decide exactly when data moves.
- **Tests:** 13 tests in 8 files, including the smoke test (a change on A shows up on B after both sync).
- **README:** how to write a scenario, the helper reference, and answers to the issue's open questions.

**Changes outside the new folder:**

- `sync-server/src/app.ts` exports its Express `app` (one line), and `package.json` gets a matching `#app` subpath import, so tests can listen on port 0 and close the server afterwards.
- `sync-server`'s `test` script runs the unit tests and then the new `test:integration` script. `typecheck` also checks `integration-tests/`.
- `sync-server/vitest.config.ts` excludes `integration-tests/` from the unit-test run.
- `lage.config.js` builds `@actual-app/api` before `sync-server`'s tests.

No loot-core code changed, and `yarn.lock` is unchanged.

**Change since the first review:** the tests first lived in a new `packages/sync-integration-tests` workspace. That changed `yarn.lock`, which triggers the Dependency Review workflow, and that workflow can't run in this fork ("Dependency review is not supported on this repository"). Commit `d66d05c1b` moved them into `sync-server`.

**AI use:** written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5).

- **AI's part:** the research on how sync works, the design, the helpers, all 13 tests, the README and this description.
- **My part:** I chose the approach (worker threads, `@actual-app/api`, location in `sync-server`), reviewed every change, and ran the commands listed under Testing.
- **AI logs:** will be added to `ai-logs/sprint3/sgstrick/` and linked here.

## Related issue(s)

Closes #161. Related to #162 (the sync scenarios that build on this setup).

The first commit (`14ee6fd86`) says `(#162)` by mistake; this PR is for #161. I didn't reword it, because that would mean force-pushing a branch that's already under review. Later commits reference #161.

## Testing

### Test Evidence

All tests are in `packages/sync-server/integration-tests/src/`. Every test runs the real sync server and real loot-core clients, so all of them are integration tests.

| Acceptance criterion                                                                                | Test(s)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Level                          | Source of expected value                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1a. Starts the real sync-server in-process on a free port, with temporary `serverFiles`/`userFiles` | `startSyncServer.test.ts` › "serves the health endpoint and cleans up on shutdown" (`/health` returns `{ status: 'UP' }` on the returned port; the account database in `serverFiles` and the `userFiles` folder exist while it runs; after `shutdown()` the port no longer answers)             | integration                    | AC; upstream behavior (`/health` response in `app.ts`)                                                                                                                                  |
| 1b. Creates an account/session and returns a valid token                                            | `startSyncServerWithBudget.test.ts` › "creates an account, a token, and an uploaded budget" (the token is accepted by `/sync/get-user-file-info`)                                                                                                                                               | integration                    | AC; upstream behavior (the server only answers that endpoint for a valid token)                                                                                                         |
| 1c. Uploads a budget and returns `fileId` and `groupId`                                             | same test: the server reports that file with the same `fileId`, `groupId` and name, `deleted: 0`                                                                                                                                                                                                | integration                    | AC; upstream behavior (`get-user-file-info` response shape)                                                                                                                             |
| 1d. **Not tested automatically, and why:**

- **AC 1d, failure path:** no test deliberately fails to check its own cleanup afterwards. **AI-written tests:** all 13 tests in `packages/sync-server/integration-tests/src/*.test.ts` were written by Claude Code. How the expected values were checked:

- They come from the ACs (for example "a change on A appears on B"), from documented server and loot-core behavior (`/health`, `get-user-file-info`, the `network-failure` reason), or from the difference a test deliberately creates. None were copied from our own code's output.

## Design Decisions

1. **One worker thread per device.** loot-core keeps its clock, database, prefs and sync state in module-level variables, so each device needs its own module graph.
   - Alternatives considered: (a) several clients in one module graph, separated with `vi.resetModules()`; (b) a child process per device.
   - Why: (a) still shares globals such as `fetch` and the SQLite handles, and depends on Vitest's module cache. (b) works but starts more slowly and needs a separate entry script and inter-process messaging. Worker threads are isolated by construction and start quickly.
   - Consequence: devices are controlled through messages (`device.request(...)`), and changes and results must be plain data.

2. **Clients go through the bundled `@actual-app/api`.**
   - Alternatives considered: (a) loot-core's internal modules directly; (b) a new client entry point inside loot-core.
   - Why: the API already supports `init` with a server URL and session token, and `downloadBudget`. Its bundle runs in a plain worker thread, which loot-core's TypeScript source can't, and (b) would change loot-core code, which the issue wanted to avoid.
   - Consequence: the API has to be built before the tests (lage does this), and devices use the API's build, not loot-core source.

3. **The setup lives in `packages/sync-server/integration-tests/`.**
   - Alternatives considered: (a) a new test-only workspace (the first version of this PR); (b) inside loot-core.
   - Why: (a) changes `yarn.lock`, which triggers the Dependency Review check that can't run in this fork. (b) would make loot-core depend on the server.
   - Consequence: sync-server doesn't list `@actual-app/api` as a dependency, so devices load `packages/api/dist/index.js` by path with hand-written types (see Tech Debt), and the starter budget is zipped without a zip library.

4. **The tests run on every `yarn test`.**
   - Alternatives considered: (a) only a separate `yarn test:integration` script; (b) a separate CI job.
   - Why: they take about 30 seconds, and if they don't run by default they stop being run. `test:integration` is still there for running them alone.
   - Consequence: `sync-server`'s tests now wait for the API build, which lage caches.

5. **Devices never sync on their own.** The worker wraps `fetch`: it blocks automatic syncs, simulates being offline, and refuses non-loopback hosts.
   - Alternatives considered: (a) let loot-core's 1-second auto-sync run and wait for it; (b) use fake timers.
   - Why: (a) makes tests timing-dependent. (b) doesn't work across worker threads, and loot-core's sync also waits on real I/O.
   - Consequence: tests must call `sync()` explicitly. Workers run with `NODE_ENV=production`, because in test mode loot-core syncs inside every change and throws when that fails.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**

- **Hand-written API types.** Devices load the built API by its path in the repo (`packages/api/dist/index.js`), and `apiBundle.ts` declares the API methods they call. These types aren't checked against the real API, so a change to one of those signatures won't fail typecheck; it would show up as a test failure. This avoids adding a dependency (and a `yarn.lock` change).
- **Own zip writer.** `zip.ts` writes uncompressed zip files so the tests don't need a zip library. It's test-only and small.
- **Vitest temp folder cleanup.** `integration-tests/vitest.globalSetup.ts` removes temp folders Vitest 5 leaves behind on Windows, using Vitest's internal `_tmpDir`. It only deletes folders directly under the OS temp directory, so if Vitest changes, it does nothing instead of deleting the wrong thing.
- **Possible leftover temp folder.** If a test times out while the server or a device is still starting up, that temporary directory isn't removed.
- **Only account changes.** `makeChange` supports account create/update/delete. More change types (transactions, categories) will be added in #162; the README explains how.
- **Workers run with `NODE_ENV=production`** to avoid loot-core's test-mode sync behavior (see Design Decision 5).

**Encountered:**

- **`yarn typecheck` overwrites the API build.** `packages/api/tsconfig.json` emits JavaScript, so a typecheck replaces the bundled `packages/api/dist/index.js` with an unbundled compile that devices can't load. Handled: lage rebuilds the API before `sync-server`'s tests, and the integration tests stop at once with "run `yarn build:api`" if the bundle is missing or overwritten. Not fixed here, because the fix belongs in the API package.
- **Dependency Review can't run in this fork.** The dependency graph isn't enabled, so any PR that changes `yarn.lock` fails. Handled by not changing `yarn.lock` (Design Decision 3).
- **Vitest 5 leaves temp folders on Windows,** in every package. Worked around for these tests only (see above).
- **`yarn lint` fails locally on Windows** because of CRLF line endings (about 505 files flagged by the formatter). It passes in CI; not changed.
- **Slow tests time out in a full `yarn test`:** loot-core `executors.test.ts` here, and `GoalReport.test.tsx` and `formula-action-integration.test.ts` in the reviewer's run. They pass on their own; not changed, since they're unrelated to this PR.
- **sync-server's `app.ts` didn't export `app`,** so it could only be started through `run()` on a fixed port. Added the export.

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.
